referenceSize.note: Aquarium 'banded trochus' (Trochus histrio, or juvenile Rochia nilotica sold as Trochus/Tectus niloticus) reaches about 3 cm basal shell diameter with a shell height about equal to the diameter (SeaLifeBase: Rochia nilotica max 15 cm shell height, common 11 cm; the trade animal is much smaller). The size gate measures the whole rest mesh across y, which is the shell's maximum basal diameter; the foot and tentacles stay inside that span.

morphology.notes: Tall, straight-sided top-shaped cone (spire angle about 62 degrees), 7.5 whorls, flat base, nearly square aperture on the right side (dextral) opening forward over the head. Shell modelled as a strict logarithmic conispiral: a quadrangular generating curve swept along a dextral helix with every whorl scaling toward the apex. Soft body: broad flat foot with a domed body hump rising into the aperture, short snout, two long cephalic tentacles with eyes at their bases, three pairs of epipodial tentacles along the foot edge (Trochidae/Tegulidae).

visualDebt: The shell is a strictly self-similar conispiral, so its base is a shallow spiral ramp (lowest at the aperture lip); the body hump fills most of the space under it but the front whorl still overhangs the mantle edge.
Beaded spiral cords, growth striae and the suture are normal-map relief only; the shell geometry itself is smooth.
No operculum, mouth or epipodial skirt is modelled; epipodial tentacles attach directly to the foot flank and the eyes are stalkless black ellipsoids.
Soft-body proportions in life position are inferred from general trochid anatomy (reference grade B for the shell, weaker for the animal).
